newsitem.title: INDIA: India RBI to keep 97/98 M3 growth at 15.0-15.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: India RBI to keep 97/98 M3 growth at 15.0-15.5 pct.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) will stick to a growth target of 15.0-15.0 percent in M3 money supply for 1997/98 (April-March), Reserve Bank of India governor Chakravarty Rangarajan said on Monday.

"Given an inflation target of 6 percent and gross domestic product growth (GDP) of 6.0-7.0 percent, we feel a M3 growth of 15.0-15.5 percent is the right rate of money supply growth," the RBI governor said.
"It is important to contain inflationary pressures as only this will lead to a sustained fall in interest rates," he said.
"So we will keep M3 growth within a 15.0 percent to 15.5 percent band."
Rangarajan was speaking at a function to launch a new deposit scheme by state-run Corporation Bank.
Year-on-year growth in M3 was 16.6 percent for the fortnight ended June 6 against 16.4 percent the previous fortnight.
Rangarajan said the projected growth in M3 will provide adequate funds to banks to increase commercial lending by around 20 percent during the current financial year.
Rangarajan said deposit growth during the current year had been good and banks should increase loan disbursals.
He said the RBI's bank rate is emerging as a signalling rate to the banking industry, referring to a series of cuts in bank prime lending rates after the central bank cuts its bank rate last week.
"The signals are being read correctly," Rangarajan said.

The RBI cut its bank rate by one percentage point when it released its monetary policy statement for first-half 1997/98 in April, and foillowed it with a second cut of one percentage point to 10.0 percent last week.
Banks have so far cut their prime lending rates by 50-150 basis points, but many have still to respond to the latest cut.
State Bank of India, the country's largest commercial bank, cut its prime rate to 13.5 percent from 14.0 percent on Saturday.
